title: Big petrol price cuts on the cards for December, and diesel could see a reprieve too - IOL
text:
Big petrol price cuts on the cards for December, and diesel could see a reprieve too Business Economy Big petrol price cuts on the cards for December, and diesel could see a reprieve too
 Jason Woosey | Published 1 day ago Ask AI 2 min A big petrol price cut is on the cards for December. 
 Image: Newspress
 Significant petrol price reductions are on the cards of December, but the diesel prices are likely to see minimal movements as Treasury's tax relief tapers off. 
 The latest data from the Central Energy Fund shows that motorists could see price cuts of R3.10 for 95 Unleaded and R2.86 for 93 Unleaded, even after factoring in the 50 cents that will be added to the equation after Treasury's temporary fuel tax reprieve is scaled back. 
 Those filling up with diesel face the return of R1.50 to the General Fuel Levy, with current data pointing to a price cut of around 37 cents for 50ppm. However, if current trends persist, the diesel over-recovery could grow further between now and month-end.
 There is a major caveat, as any escalation of conflict in the Middle East could see oil prices rising rapidly once again. 
 The projected price decreases for December come as a direct result of lower international oil prices, with benchmark Brent crude having tumbled by around 15% following major Republican losses in the US midterm elections, settling below the $100 per barrel mark this week. 
 “Brent crude is holding near $98/barrel, marginally softer, after US President Donald Trump signalled fresh Iran strikes are unlikely should talks progress, draining some of oil’s risk premium,” said Bianca Botes, managing director at Citadel Global. 
 However, Investec chief economist Annabel Bishop cautioned that the longer-term outlook for transport costs remains clouded by current realities and near-term hurdles. 
 “Freight rates rose to record highs last month for oil shipping, with oil stocks very low and little near-term chance of rebuilding inventories. Transport costs for tankers are at record highs, while other logistics costs such as insurance have climbed steeply.” 
 The projected fuel price cuts also arrive at a time when South Africans are paying record prices for petrol and diesel. 
 While the beginning of November saw petrol prices cut by one cent and diesel by between R1.10 and R1.20, petrol has risen by almost R10 per litre this year, while diesel has gone up by around R13, after the US war on Iran created extreme volatility in international oil markets.
